_why: CI jobs accrete one unremarkable job at a time, and nothing says anything at the moment
each is added. This repo does NOT currently have that problem — the census at authoring
time was 7 PR-reachable jobs, 3 required, 6 relevance-gated, 0 freeloaders. The ratchet
exists so that stays true by construction rather than by discipline.
Adapted from loom#1877 (kailash-rs), whose measured instance was 33 PR-reachable jobs
against a pool of 24 with only 12 gating anything.
_declaration_is_the_contract: Adding a PR-reachable job means adding it HERE too, as one of: a required context, a
relevance-gated job (a job-level `if:` or a `paths:` filter on the pull_request arm), or
a budgeted exemption below with a dated rationale. The audit fails otherwise. That is the
whole mechanism: the cost of a new job becomes a visible, reviewable line in a diff.

capacity_note: DELIBERATELY null, not a guessed number. Concurrent-job capacity for GitHub-hosted
runners is a property of the ACCOUNT PLAN, readable only via an endpoint no configured
secret here can reach (the same gap loom#1877 records as its decision point 3: the
capacity number has no scheduled reader).
A declared-but-unverified integer would be an instrument that cannot discriminate — it
would render a green 'within capacity' verdict from a number nobody measured. So the
audit reports capacity as UNKNOWN and does NOT emit a pass for it. The freeloader check
below is fully decidable from the workflow files and is the gate that actually bites.
To activate the capacity check: set capacity to the measured integer and change
capacity_source to how it was obtained (e.g. 'gh api /orgs/<org>/settings/billing/...',
with the date). The audit picks it up with no code change.

_budgeted_shape.job: the job's `name:` (or its id when unnamed), exactly as the audit reports it
_budgeted_shape.rationale: why this job runs on every PR while gating nothing
_budgeted_shape.revisit: YYYY-MM-DD — an exemption with no revisit date is how a temporary allowance becomes permanent
